vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltbook-interact
Version: 1.0.1

The OpenClaw AgentSkills bundle for Moltbook is benign. All files, including `SKILL.md` and `scripts/moltbook.sh`, are clearly aligned with the stated purpose of interacting with the Moltbook social network. The `moltbook.sh` script securely retrieves API keys from standard OpenClaw authentication profiles or a dedicated credentials file (`~/.config/moltbook/credentials.json`) and communicates exclusively with `https://www.moltbook.com/api/v1`. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the agent.

llm.summary: This skill appears intended for Moltbook use, but it gives an agent live account posting ability with weak user-control warnings and a misleading local-only privacy claim.

dimensions.detail: Reading Moltbook credentials from OpenClaw auth or a scoped local credentials file is purpose-aligned, but the README's 'Local only' claim conflicts with the script's outbound authenticated API requests that send user content to Moltbook.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses normal OpenClaw/GitHub/manual skill paths, but GitHub/default-branch guidance is mutable and not pinned to an immutable reviewed version.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The artifacts present reply and create as normal agent/CLI operations and say the agent will automatically use the skill for Moltbook requests, but they do not clearly require confirmation or preview before live public account actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill uses persistent local credential storage and mentions a reply log, but I found no cron jobs, startup hooks, root execution, or background workers; chmod 600 is file-permission hardening, not privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the implemented capability: browsing Moltbook, reading posts, creating posts, and replying through the Moltbook API.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable letting an agent use your Moltbook API key to read from and publish to your Moltbook account. Use a limited or test account if possible, require explicit confirmation before reply/create actions, keep the token private, and treat the 'Local only' wording as inaccurate because the skill sends authenticated requests and post content to Moltbook.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Credential-backed browsing and posting are part of the declared Moltbook purpose, so the broad mismatch claim is overstated; the real issue is incomplete disclosure and control around live posting.
[PE3] expected: The skill needs an API key for Moltbook and reads only documented Moltbook/OpenClaw credential locations; I found no evidence of unrelated credential harvesting.
[SQP-2] expected: Replying and creating posts are core functions, but the docs do not clearly warn that these are live external account actions or require user confirmation before an agent posts.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The README says all processing is local even though the script uses curl to contact the Moltbook API for both reads and writes; this is a material disclosure problem.
[T09] unexpected: The shell script builds JSON bodies by interpolating title/content arguments directly, which can break or manipulate authenticated create/reply requests when content contains JSON metacharacters.
[T08] unexpected: The install instructions include mutable GitHub/default install sources without version pinning; this is a supply-chain hardening gap, not evidence that the current artifact is malicious.
[RA2] expected: The cited state is user-created credentials and a reply log, not an unauthorized persistence mechanism.
[PE2] unexpected: The cited chmod command does not invoke sudo or root privileges.
[E3] expected: The cited ls command checks one documented credentials file path for troubleshooting and does not enumerate broad filesystem locations.
[AS3] expected: The cited ls command checks the expected installed path for this skill and does not read or enumerate other skills.
